```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use the signed-in visitor's Microsoft account to query Azure SQL with DBI
or dbplyr. This example lists the database tables they can see.

## Set up access

Install `odbc` and Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server. Your database
administrator must enable [Microsoft Entra authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/authentication-aad-configure?view=azuresql)
and give users or their groups database access.

Create a Microsoft Entra Web app registration with delegated SQL access,
and register `http://localhost:8100` as its redirect URI. The
`services = "sql"` preset below requests the SQL token for you.

Put your registration's values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R` and replace the example connection settings:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "sql",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_azure_sql(
    auth$connection,
    server = "example.database.windows.net",
    database = "Reporting"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT TOP (20) name FROM sys.tables")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` in that directory, then open
`http://localhost:8100` and sign in. The output waits for sign-in and clears
when you sign out.

## Query your own tables

Create `con` inside `server()`, passing `auth$connection` without
parentheses. Call `con()` in a render or reactive expression before querying.
The helper reuses the connection and closes it when the authorization or
Shiny session ends.

For an `Orders` table, you could replace the output with a dbplyr query:

```{r dbplyr-query}
output$rows <- renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  dplyr::tbl(connection, "Orders") |>
    dplyr::filter(amount > 100) |>
    dplyr::collect()
})
```

Install `dbplyr` and `dplyr` for this alternative. Use DBI parameter binding
when a SQL query includes values supplied by visitors.

## Other SQL Server deployments

For SQL Managed Instance or Synapse SQL, supply that deployment's server
and database to `oauth_db_azure_sql()`. For SQL Server configured to accept
Entra tokens, use `oauth_db_sql_server()` with the same arguments and client.

Driver options such as `driver`, `port`, and `timeout` are documented in
`?oauth_db_azure_sql`. For custom permissions or an existing login, see
[Authentication and sessions](authorization.html).
